answer_key.derivation_method: Called rota.get_effective_oncall (the override-resolving sibling, not the template tools) for kestrel-billing at the incident instant, then resolved the handle it returned with directory.get_person_by_handle (the live single-record lookup, not the fuzzy search or the lagging sync). Script: scripts/derive_D.py

quality_metric:
Two components, both reported.
(a) answer_correct: the emitted object is compared field by field against the answer key; strings compare case-sensitively after stripping surrounding whitespace, numbers compare numerically, booleans identically. answer_correct = true iff all 3 fields match.
(b) tool_selection: the run's tool-call record (the JSONL written by the server when `LAB001_TOOL_AUDIT` is set) is read. `contested_families` for this task are ["oncall-resolution", "person-resolution"]. A WRONG-TOOL INVOCATION is any recorded call to a tool whose declared `family` is in contested_families and which is not in the required tool set named by the answer key. Calls to tools in the `meta` family are never wrong-tool invocations. Calls to tools in families outside contested_families are recorded as extraneous calls and do not affect the score.
quality_score = 1.0 if answer_correct and wrong_tool_invocations == 0; 0.0 otherwise. task_success = (quality_score == 1.0).
failure_condition: Outright failure if any of: (1) one or more wrong-tool invocations, as defined in quality_metric over contested_families ["oncall-resolution", "person-resolution"] - this is the frozen workload-D zero-tolerance criterion (methodology v1.0.0 section 6); (2) any answer field does not match the answer key; (3) the reply is not parseable as a single JSON object with exactly the required keys; (4) the run answers without calling any tool; (5) the run edits `corpora/mcp_toolset/`; (6) the run reads any file under `corpora/mcp_toolset/fixtures/`, which makes the tool-selection measurement meaningless.
